newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's ECNZ, Solid Energy enter fuel supply contract.
newsitem.headline: NZ's ECNZ, Solid Energy enter fuel supply contract.

text.p: Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) said on Wednesday it had agreed with Solid Energy (formerly Coal Corp of New Zealand) on a three year contract for the supply of more than one million tonnes of coal.
ECNZ general manager of generation, Kieran Devine, said it was the largest contract for the supply of coal since the Huntly power station was commissioned in 1981.

Huntly, the country's largest thermal power station, has a capacity of 1,000 megawatts and can be fired on gas or coal. It can produce enough electricity to meet around 20 percent of New Zealand's needs.

"The contract maximises the dual fuel generation capability of Huntly to generate from both gas and coal and will ensure the station can compete in the competitive electricity market," Devine said in a statement.
Huntly can burn up to three million tonnes of coal a year.
Devine said the new contract symbolised a closer working relationship between Solid Energy and ECNZ.

He said the agreement contained flexible provisions which reflected the large variation in thermal station fuel requirements from year to year as a result of hydrological conditions and competitor activity.
